name: Ruadh

attributes.attribute: linked with women in legend and daily work

sources: Gwynn, Edward. The Metrical Dindshenchas. Part II. Vol. IX. Royal Irish Academy, Todd Lecture Series. Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, and Co., Ltd., 1906–1924, 27–35.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ruadh and Bó Duh stand for the red cow and the black cow. Cows were linked with women both in legend and in daily life. Women did the milking, churned the butter, and looked after the herd in the summer grazing. The pairing of cow and woman ran through farming life in the region.

okr.objective: Record the red and black cows and their tie to women in Celtic farm life.
key_results: Ruadh stands for the red cow.
Bó Duh stands for the black cow.
Women milked cows and churned the butter.
Women tended the herd in summer pastures.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
